package_info.why_malicious: The package exposes an exported activity (TagViewer) that can be triggered by any app without permissions, allowing a rogue app to spoof NFC tag reads and present arbitrary content to the user, potentially leading to phishing, social engineering, or other attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when malicious app chooses to execute)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious app code (not in com.android.apps.tag, but abuses its exported activity)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code constructs a fake NDEF message (e.g., a malicious URL), crafts an Intent targeting the exported TagViewer activity, and launches it, causing the system to display a 'new tag scanned' popup with attacker-controlled content.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows any app to simulate an NFC tag scan and present arbitrary content to the user via a system UI, bypassing the need for actual NFC hardware or user intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only genuine NFC tag scans should trigger the TagViewer, and only with data from real tags. Here, any app can trigger the UI with arbitrary data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use NFC intents for genuine tag reading, but should not spoof tags or trigger system UIs without user action.
key_indicators: Direct invocation of exported system activity with crafted data
No permissions required to trigger sensitive UI
Ability to inject arbitrary NDEF messages

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user scans a real NFC tag and malicious app is installed)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious app code (intent filter for ACTION_NDEF_DISCOVERED)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a real NFC tag is scanned, the malicious app intercepts the intent, modifies the tag content (e.g., changes a phone number), and forwards the altered data to the TagViewer, causing the user to see attacker-controlled information instead of the real tag data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying NFC tag data before it reaches the system UI is a clear violation of user expectations and can be used for phishing or fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users expect to see the real content of scanned NFC tags, not attacker-modified data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may process NFC tags for their own use, but should not alter and forward them to system UIs as if they were genuine.
key_indicators: Intent filter for high-priority NFC actions
Modification of tag data in transit
Forwarding to system UI with spoofed content

attack_chain.action: Malicious app registers for NFC intents (e.g., ACTION_NDEF_DISCOVERED) to intercept tag scans or triggers TagViewer directly.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is presented with attacker-controlled content in the system UI.

attack_chain.action: User sees a 'new tag scanned' popup with attacker-supplied data (e.g., malicious URL, phone number, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: User may interact with the content, leading to phishing, fraud, or other attacks.

attack_chain.action: If user clicks the link or initiates a call, the attacker's payload is executed (e.g., browser opens malicious site, call is placed to attacker-controlled number).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: user compromise, phishing, or social engineering.

behavioral_signatures: Apps sending explicit intents to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with crafted NDEF messages
Apps registering for ACTION_NDEF_DISCOVERED and modifying tag data before forwarding
Unexpected 'new tag scanned' popups without actual NFC activity
file_indicators: App code invoking startActivity with com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer as target
network_indicators: NDEF messages containing suspicious URLs (e.g., phishing domains)
NDEF messages with phone numbers not matching expected tag content
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that register for high-priority NFC intents and forward modified NDEF messages to system activities. Flag apps that invoke com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with crafted data, especially if no actual NFC hardware event occurred. Alert on repeated 'new tag scanned' popups without corresponding NFC activity, or on NDEF messages containing known malicious URLs or phone numbers.
